text:
mike-infra: FYI rolling BIOS+BMC microcode to eu-west1 gpu-rack pool triggered OOB timeouts on 8/32 hosts, provisioning failing. Seen SecureBoot flip to 'enabled' on 3 hosts unexpectedly.
asha-sre: WTF, secureboot toggling during firmware update? Any logs?
ben-eng: saw same — provisioner shows `waiting_for_console` and ipmi timeouts. grabbing `oobctl` output now.
jamal-oncall: tagging @sre-bot to pull recent deploys and canary status. Can we pause the rollout? :point_up:
sre-bot: deploy-diff detected: firmware/bmc-v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 applied to eu-west1-canary-*/gpu-* at 2026-03-18T09:12Z. Canary failures: 2/3.
mike-infra: Pausing rollout across eu-west1. Runbook step 1: add `bmc::skip=true` label to pending hosts and stop the waves.
ben-eng: adding label now. running `kubectl label nodes --selector=hw=rack-eu1 bmc.skip=true` (one-liner).
asha-sre: logs attached: ```
Mar 18 09:18:12 ipmi[1234]: conn_timeout rc=110 host=10.11.22.33
Mar 18 09:18:13 bmc-updater[456]: verify_secure_boot: new_flag=true from vendor fw
Mar 18 09:18:14 provisioner[789]: waiting_for_console: timeout=600
``` 
olivia-platform: if SecureBoot flips mid-provision the kernel chain will reject our PXE image. That explains provisioning stalls. Any idea why fw set it? vendor notes mention a new default-on policy in v1.12.4 for certain BMC SKUs.
jamal-oncall: impacted pools: gpu-eu-west1-a (8 nodes degraded), spare-capacity down by ~25%, autoscaler keeps spinning up more preemptibles -> cost spike. I've limited autoscaler for now.
ben-eng: can we temporarily route new allocations to us-west1? latency-sensitive jobs will degrade; but at least clusters won't queue.
mike-infra: yes, start soft-routing for non-interactive batches only. Olivia, can you update routing policy and add capacity cap?
olivia-platform: on it. I'll push a policy: `route: prefer us-west1 unless tag=low-latency` and cap eu-west1 to 70% of baseline. Deploying in 2m.
asha-sre: what's the rollback plan? vendor provided a bmc flash tool but it needs serial/OOB. If OOB is flaky we might need onsite intervention or vendor remote session.
ben-eng: running `oobctl flash --image bmc-v1.12.2 --targets @eu-west1-degraded --force --reboot` but half the hosts fail with IPMI handshake error.
jamal-oncall: opening incident INC-20260318-1 and paging vendor support. tagging on-call tech. Include MACs and serials.
ben-eng: workaround for now: mark affected hosts as drained and set `provisioner.allow_fallback_images=true` so some workloads can still go to older images via manual provisioning.
mike-infra: good. Also enable KV cache warmup on healthy nodes to reduce churn: `runtime.cache.prefix=true`.
asha-sre: quick check — any certs/HSM expiries around that time? SecureBoot toggle could be triggered by cert verification fail.
olivia-platform: no cert expiries in the window, I checked KMS logs. Vendor microcode change seems likely.
jamal-oncall: vendor response ETA 30m. They suspect the release toggles secure boot for SKU batch with new silicon. They've paused their release.
ben-eng: creating a small script to detect SecureBoot drift and auto-exclude nodes before they get reprovisioned: ```
#!/bin/bash
for n in $(oobctl list --status reachable --region eu-west1 --format id); do
  sb=$(oobctl get $n secureboot)
  if [ "$sb" = "enabled" ]; then
    oobctl tag $n degraded:secureboot_drift
    provisioner drain $n --reason "secureboot drift"
  fi
done
``` 
asha-sre: love it. Add an alert to paging channel if >2 nodes flip in 10m.
mike-infra: Agree. Ben, Olivia — coordinate on rollback vs vendor fix. Jamal — keep autoscaler restricted and update finance on cost impact.
olivia-platform: rollback requires serial consoles for ~6 hosts. Vendor offered remote flash for 4; remaining 2 need onsite vendor or our field tech. Scheduling now.
jamal-oncall: FYI current provisional cost burn estimate: +12% hours due to extra preemptible replacements. Finance notified (ticket FIN-587).
nash-sre: minor nit: can we avoid toggles by setting `bmc.force_secureboot=false` in provisioner until we have a safe firmware?
ben-eng: that bypasses hardware-level assertions, but helps boot for now. I'll sync with security.
mike-infra: security sign-off required. @asha-sre loop in sec for temp exception.
asha-sre: pinging sec group. provisional exception approved for eu-west1 for 6h with audit log.
ben-eng: implemented `bmc.force_secureboot=false` on provisioner canary and pushed audit event.
jamal-oncall: vendor remote flash started for 4 hosts. monitoring OOB recovery.
sre-bot: update: 4/8 hosts recovered OOB, 2 hosts still unreachable, secureboot drift count = 3.
mike-infra: good progress. Keep this thread focused. After vendor verifies image we can plan a safer re-roll with canary size x3 and pre-flash checks.
asha-sre: postmortem items: stricter canary gating, pre-check for secureboot flag change, autoscaler hysteresis to avoid cost spikes. I'll draft the follow-up RFC.
ben-eng: adding runbook note: if OOB unreachable for >20m, auto-fail to region routing and open incident.
jamal-oncall: incident updated: INC-20260318-1 -> severity: high -> status: mitigation. Next update in 15m. :alarm_clock:
mike-infra: thanks everyone. I'll compile checklist and schedule vendor debrief. Keep monitoring and only allow manual rollouts until we confirm fix.
